text:
Sam Patel: FYI CI evals for the new llama-3q8 quant build spiked a 12% metric delta on our 'cc_quality' metric after yesterday's runner change. Error seen when running prompt binding. @sahil any idea? :eyes:

Sahil Menon: saw alerts. Reproducer locally shows runner process exits on some prompt sets, looks like a mismatch in tokenizer/seq alignment. PID logs attached.

Michelle Zhao: dev-deploy-bot indicates the change was  PR #4125 - 'runner: prefer-utf8-prompt-binding' merged by jordan. Might be related. :grimacing:

jordan: yeah that PR touched prompt normalization before tokenization. I added a guard but maybe we're double-normalizing for some datasets. Will investigate.

Sam Patel: logs:
```bash
EVAL_RUNNER: AssertionError: input length mismatch (tok_len=128, expected=126)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner.py", line 442, in process
    tokens = tokenizer.encode(normalized)
AssertionError: input length mismatch
```

Michelle Zhao: ci-bot shows failing job: eval-quant-ci/metrics-check → job 5821. Link: https://ci.internal/reports/5821

ci-bot: build 5821 failed: metric_delta_threshold_exceeded (cc_quality +12.3%). Suggest running bisect job: `python tools/bisect_eval_changes.py --suite=cc_quality --since=origin/main~20`

Sahil Menon: I'll kick the bisect. If the regression tracks to the PR we should hold the release and revert.

jordan: repro confirmed with dataset 'customer_support_short'. I can make a quick branch that removes normalization; want me to open a revert or a fix?

Sam Patel: Hold release for Dedicated and Hosted canary. Michelle please pause canary rollouts. @michelle

Michelle Zhao: Paused canaries. Also opened a dashboard alert on historical window. :white_check_mark:

Sahil Menon: bisect output (summary):
```text
candidate PRs:
 - origin/main~15 .. origin/main: no regression
 - PR #4125 -> regression introduced
```

Sahil Menon: Bisect points to PR #4125. Propose revert merge and re-run full eval suite. Thoughts?

jordan: ack. I'll open revert PR now: #4132

Sam Patel: If revert is risky, another option: patch runner to detect double-normalized input and fallback to original tokenization (short patch). Which is faster to ship?

jordan: revert is fastest to get back to green. Patch will need more tests.

Sam Patel: Ok revert then. @michelle coordinate with releases to block the deploy. @sahil re-run the evals after revert and paste results here.

Michelle Zhao: Revert PR #4132 opened and queued. Releases notified. :pray:

ci-bot: revert PR passed unit + integration. Will run eval CI next.

Sahil Menon: Post-revert evals: cc_quality delta -> +0.4% (within threshold). All other metrics nominal.

Sam Patel: Great. Leaving a follow-up action item: add a tokenization end-to-end test in eval CI covering normalization pipeline. I'll create a tracker ticket.

jordan: sorry about the break. adding test now.

Sam Patel: Thanks everyone. Closing thread when release unblocks.
